Tiêu đề đề bài: Task 2.1: Advantages and Disadvantages of Urbanization
Nội dung chi tiết:
Read the following statement:

"Urbanization is proceeding at an unprecedented rate worldwide, drawing vast populations from rural districts into metropolises in pursuit of better living standards. While rapid urbanization fosters economic vitality and modern convenience, it simultaneously spawns critical issues such as overcrowding, environmental degradation, and overloaded public infrastructure."

Write an essay to an educated reader examining both the advantages and disadvantages of rapid urbanization. Support your arguments with specific reasons and illustrative examples.
title: Task 2.1: Advantages and Disadvantages of Urbanization
content:
Read the following statement:

"Urbanization is proceeding at an unprecedented rate worldwide, drawing vast populations from rural districts into metropolises in pursuit of better living standards. While rapid urbanization fosters economic vitality and modern convenience, it simultaneously spawns critical issues such as overcrowding, environmental degradation, and overloaded public infrastructure."

Write an essay to an educated reader examining both the advantages and disadvantages of rapid urbanization. Support your arguments with specific reasons and illustrative examples.

body1.example: For instance, in many big cities today, young workers from rural areas can easily find office jobs, use modern hospitals, and send their children to well-equipped schools. As a result, their family income grows and their daily life becomes much more comfortable.
body1.frame: Mở: On the one hand, rapid urbanization brings a lot of advantages in several ways | Ruột ĐOẠN 1 | Chốt: Clearly, these benefits make rapid urbanization appealing to many people.
body1.point: A very important point to consider is that rapid urbanization helps boost economic development and improve people's living standard. This means that residents have more opportunities to find well-paid jobs and grow their careers. Another point I would like to make is that big cities offer modern public facilities and convenient services. This is because of the fact that governments and companies invest heavily in hospitals, schools, and fast public transport in urban areas.

body2.example: For example, many residents often face long traffic jams during rush hour and breathe polluted air every morning. If this issue is ignored, it will cause serious health problems and lower the quality of city life.
body2.frame: Mở: On the other hand, the disadvantages of rapid urbanization are undeniable | Ruột ĐOẠN 2 | Chốt: It is clear that overcrowding and pollution can create serious drawbacks if ignored.
body2.point: In fact, rapid urbanization puts heavy pressure on housing, roads, and public services. This happens because when too many people move into one city, it easily leads to traffic jams, overloaded hospitals, and high living costs. In addition, crowded streets and thousands of vehicles release harmful exhaust fumes, which damage the environment and make city dwellers feel stressed.

hint.conclusion: In conclusion, rapid urbanization brings both pros and cons. While people can benefit from better job opportunities and modern services, they also need to handle overcrowding, air pollution, and overloaded public services. Therefore, both individuals and local authorities should work together to make the most of rapid urbanization responsibly.

intro.ld1: find better jobs and improve their living standard
intro.ld2: overcrowding, air pollution, and overloaded public services

Tiêu đề đề bài: Task 2.2: Advantages and Disadvantages of Taking a Gap Year
Nội dung chi tiết:
Read the following statement:

"Taking a gap year—a year off between graduating from high school and starting university to travel or work—has gained immense popularity among young people. While proponents argue that a gap year provides practical life skills and personal maturity, critics worry it causes academic disruption and financial burdens."

Write an essay to an educated reader discussing both the advantages and disadvantages of taking a gap year before entering higher education. Support your arguments with specific reasons and illustrative examples.
title: Task 2.2: Advantages and Disadvantages of Taking a Gap Year
content:
Read the following statement:

"Taking a gap year—a year off between graduating from high school and starting university to travel or work—has gained immense popularity among young people. While proponents argue that a gap year provides practical life skills and personal maturity, critics worry it causes academic disruption and financial burdens."

Write an essay to an educated reader discussing both the advantages and disadvantages of taking a gap year before entering higher education. Support your arguments with specific reasons and illustrative examples.

body1.example: For instance, my brother was unsure which major to choose after finishing high school. Therefore, he decided to take a gap year to work part-time at a local café and join a volunteer group. As a result, he finally became more independent and picked a career he truly loved. If he had not taken that year off, he would not have been so confident at university.
body1.focus: Advantages of taking a gap year
body1.frame: Mở: On the one hand, taking a gap year before starting university brings a lot of advantages in several ways | Ruột ĐOẠN 1 | Chốt: Clearly, these benefits make taking a gap year appealing to many people.
body1.point: A very important point to consider is that taking a gap year helps young people learn practical life skills and become more independent. This means that working or traveling in a new environment teaches them to manage their own money and solve daily problems on their own. Another point I would like to make is that students can broaden their mind and choose the right university major. This is because of the fact that real-life experience helps them understand their real interests and adjust smoothly to the social environment.

body2.example: For example, I was tempted to take a year off to travel with friends right after graduation. For this reason, I got to talk with my older cousin who had done it and struggled to catch up in university math classes. If I had not listened to his story, I would not have been able to know that a gap year without a clear plan can slow down my studies.
body2.focus: Disadvantages of taking a gap year
body2.frame: Mở: On the other hand, the disadvantages of taking a gap year before starting university are undeniable | Ruột ĐOẠN 2 | Chốt: It is clear that delayed graduation and extra pressure can create serious drawbacks if ignored.
body2.point: In fact, pausing formal study for a whole year can disrupt a student's learning habits and delay graduation behind their peers. This happens because when young people stay away from school for too long, it easily leads to forgetting basic lessons and losing focus in class. In addition, traveling or doing unpaid internships can cost a great deal of money, placing extra financial pressure on parents.

hint.conclusion: In conclusion, taking a gap year before starting university brings both pros and cons. While people can benefit from learning practical life skills and broadening their mind, they also need to handle delayed graduation and extra financial or study pressure. Therefore, both individuals and schools should work together to make the most of taking a gap year responsibly.

intro.ld1: learn practical life skills and broaden their mind
intro.ld2: delaying graduation and facing extra financial or study pressure

Nội dung chi tiết:
Read the following statement:

"An increasing number of parents today choose to purchase personal smartphones for their young children so they can stay in touch and access educational apps. However, other parents argue that giving children their own smartphones exposes them to harmful online content and screen addiction."

Write an essay to an educated reader discussing both views on allowing children to own personal smartphones and present your own perspective. Support your arguments with specific reasons and illustrative examples.
group: Đề thi thực tế AJC 07/11/2026 (Sáng - Ca 2)
title: Task 2.3: Permitting Children to Own Personal Smartphones
content:
Read the following statement:

"An increasing number of parents today choose to purchase personal smartphones for their young children so they can stay in touch and access educational apps. However, other parents argue that giving children their own smartphones exposes them to harmful online content and screen addiction."

Write an essay to an educated reader discussing both views on allowing children to own personal smartphones and present your own perspective. Support your arguments with specific reasons and illustrative examples.

body1.example: For instance, my brother was worried when his ten-year-old son walked home from extra classes in the evening. Therefore, he decided to buy him a simple smartphone with a learning app. As a result, he finally felt calmer because he could call his son anytime and check his daily progress. If he had not given his son that phone, he would not have been able to reach him quickly.
body1.focus: View 1: Why some support giving children personal smartphones
body1.frame: Mở: First and foremost, people should recognize why some support giving young children personal smartphones | Ruột ĐOẠN 1 | Chốt: Clearly, this perspective has reasonable points.
body1.point: A very important point to consider is that owning a personal smartphone makes communication between parents and children fast and convenient. This means that busy parents can easily call or message their kids to make sure they are safe after school. Another point I would like to make is that smartphones give young learners quick access to useful study apps. This is because of the fact that children can practice English vocabulary and watch short educational videos anytime at home.

body2.example: For example, I was surprised to see my younger cousin spend four hours every night playing mobile games after getting his own phone at age nine. For this reason, I got to talk with my aunt about setting strict daily screen limits for him. If I had not seen how tired he looked in class, I would not have been able to know that early phone ownership can harm a child so quickly.
body2.focus: View 2 (Preferred): Why waiting until children are older is better
body2.frame: Mở: On the other hand, there are stronger arguments in support of waiting until children are older before giving them personal smartphones | Ruột ĐOẠN 2 | Chốt: It is clear that waiting until children are older is a more practical choice.
body2.point: In fact, giving young children their own smartphones often leads to screen addiction and exposure to harmful online content. This happens because when kids lack proper guidance and self-control, it easily leads to watching violent videos, copying bad habits, and losing focus on schoolwork. In addition, staring at screens for hours harms children's eyesight and reduces face-to-face interaction with family members.

hint.conclusion: In conclusion, although both views have reasonable points, I prefer waiting until children are older before giving them personal smartphones because it allows people to protect children from harmful online content and build healthier daily habits. Therefore, both individuals and schools should work together to make the most of smartphone use responsibly.

intro.debai: allowing young children to own personal smartphones
intro.ld1: protect children from harmful online content and screen addiction
intro.ld2: better concentration and healthier daily habits

body.frame: D. Provide Information (I would like to let you know that...)

Tiêu đề đề bài: Task 2.4: Educational Benefits of Historical Exhibitions at Public Libraries
Nội dung chi tiết:
Read the following statement:

"The Hanoi Public Library is hosting a special historical exhibition showcasing rare historical archives, books, and photographs about the August Revolution, President Ho Chi Minh, and Vietnam's national liberation struggle. Some people think that in the digital era, people rarely visit physical exhibitions anymore."

Write an essay to an educated reader explaining the educational and cultural benefits of visiting this historical exhibition, and encourage citizens, particularly young students, to attend. Support your arguments with specific reasons and illustrative examples.
title: Task 2.4: Educational Benefits of Historical Exhibitions at Public Libraries
content:
Read the following statement:

"The Hanoi Public Library is hosting a special historical exhibition showcasing rare historical archives, books, and photographs about the August Revolution, President Ho Chi Minh, and Vietnam's national liberation struggle. Some people think that in the digital era, people rarely visit physical exhibitions anymore."

Write an essay to an educated reader explaining the educational and cultural benefits of visiting this historical exhibition, and encourage citizens, particularly young students, to attend. Support your arguments with specific reasons and illustrative examples.

body1.example: For instance, my brother was bored with reading short history summaries on his phone before his high school exam. Therefore, he decided to visit the historical exhibition at the Hanoi Public Library on Sunday morning. As a result, he finally understood the August Revolution clearly after seeing real old newspapers and wartime letters. If he had not visited the exhibition, he would not have been so excited about learning history.
body1.focus: Educational benefits of visiting the historical exhibition
body1.frame: Mở: First and foremost, people should recognize that visiting this historical exhibition brings clear educational value | Ruột ĐOẠN 1 | Chốt: Clearly, gaining deeper historical knowledge brings undeniable value in modern life.
body1.point: A very important point to consider is that visiting the exhibition at the Hanoi Public Library helps students broaden their mind beyond quick online searches. This means that seeing rare archives, original books, and photographs about President Ho Chi Minh and the August Revolution makes history feel real and easy to remember. Another point I would like to make is that physical exhibitions provide rich knowledge and experience in a quiet, focused setting. This is because of the fact that visitors can read carefully and ask library guides questions without digital distractions.

body2.example: For example, I was invited to join a weekend group visit to the Hanoi Public Library with my university club last month. For this reason, I got to discuss Vietnam's national liberation struggle with my friends and share photos to invite other students. If I had not attended that event in person, I would not have been able to know that a library exhibition could inspire such strong national pride.
body2.focus: Cultural benefits and encouraging young citizens to attend
body2.frame: Mở: Secondly, there are further arguments in support of the idea that visiting this exhibition builds cultural pride and encourages young people to connect | Ruột ĐOẠN 2 | Chốt: It is clear that building cultural pride plays an important role.
body2.point: In fact, attending this historical exhibition builds a strong sense of belonging and deepens respect for Vietnam's heritage. This happens because when young students explore national history together through face-to-face interaction, it easily leads to meaningful conversations and shared national pride. In addition, encouraging citizens, especially students, to visit helps keep public libraries lively and preserves cultural memories in the digital era.

hint.conclusion: In conclusion, I strongly agree that visiting the historical exhibition at the Hanoi Public Library brings clear educational and cultural benefits, mainly because it helps students gain deeper historical knowledge and supports national pride. Therefore, both individuals and schools should work together to make the most of public historical exhibitions responsibly.

intro.debai: visiting the historical exhibition at the Hanoi Public Library in the digital era
intro.ld1: gain deeper historical knowledge beyond short online articles
intro.ld2: build national pride and encourage young students to connect with heritage
